candidates.workingClaim: December 26, 1967: On December 26, 1967, the Wham-O Manufacturing Company was issued a US patent for what it called a saucer-shaped throwing implement, better known as the Frisbee.
December 26, 1893: On December 26, 1893, Mao Zedong was born. A Marxist theorist and revolutionary, he became the first chairman of the People's Republic of China, serving from 1949 to 1959.
December 26, 2004: On December 26, 2004, a massive earthquake shook the Indian Ocean floor west of the island of Sumatra, triggering a devastating tsunami that struck coastlines across the region.
December 26, 1791: On December 26, 1791, the mathematician and inventor Charles Babbage, a pioneer of mechanical computing, was born in London.
December 26, 1908: On December 26, 1908, Jack Johnson defeated Tommy Burns in Sydney, Australia, to become the first Black fighter to win the world heavyweight boxing championship.
December 27, 537: On December 27, 537, the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople was consecrated as a church. It was then the largest church in the world.
December 27, 1831: On December 27, 1831, Charles Darwin set sail on HMS Beagle, beginning the voyage during which he would formulate his theory of evolution.
December 27, 1571: On December 27, 1571, the German astronomer Johannes Kepler was born. He discovered three major laws of planetary motion.
December 27, 1949: On December 27, 1949, the Dutch formally relinquished control over Indonesia, which had declared its independence in 1945.
December 27, 2007: On December 27, 2007, Benazir Bhutto, former prime minister of Pakistan, was assassinated in Rawalpindi while campaigning in parliamentary elections.
December 28, 1895: On December 28, 1895, the first public demonstration of the Lumiere brothers' Cinematographe took place at the Grand Cafe in Paris, a landmark in the birth of cinema.

December 28, 1065: On December 28, 1065, the new abbey church that Edward the Confessor had built at Westminster was consecrated. The king was too ill to attend the service and died about a week later.
December 28, 1885: On December 28, 1885, the first session of the Indian National Congress convened. The party later led the movement for India's independence.
December 28, 1918: On December 28, 1918, Constance Markievicz became the first woman elected to the British House of Commons.
December 28, 1973: On December 28, 1973, US President Richard Nixon signed the Endangered Species Act into law.
December 29, 1937: On December 29, 1937, with the enactment of a new constitution, the Irish Free State became known as Ireland.

December 29, 1845: On December 29, 1845, Texas, until then an independent republic, legally entered the Union as a US state when Congress accepted its state constitution. Congress had passed the annexation resolution on February 28, 1845.
December 29, 1809: On December 29, 1809, William Ewart Gladstone was born in Liverpool. He served as prime minister of Great Britain four times between 1868 and 1894.
December 29, 1890: On December 29, 1890, US Army troops carried out the Wounded Knee Massacre in South Dakota. It was the last major armed conflict between the United States and the Plains peoples.
December 29, 2015: On December 29, 2015, the World Health Organization declared Guinea free of Ebola, some two years after the deadly disease was reported in the country.
December 30, 1922: On December 30, 1922, the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was established, with its capital in Moscow.
December 30, 1896: On December 30, 1896, Jose Rizal, the writer and reformer regarded as a national hero of the Philippines, was publicly executed by the country's Spanish rulers.
December 30, 1853: On December 30, 1853, the United States acquired nearly 30,000 square miles of northern Mexican territory with the signing of the Gadsden Purchase.
December 30, 1902: On December 30, 1902, the British explorer Robert Falcon Scott set a new record for reaching the farthest point south, on the Ross Ice Shelf.
December 30, 1803: On December 30, 1803, the Maratha chief Daulat Rao Sindhia signed the Treaty of Surji-Arjungaon, ceding political power and territory in India to the British.
December 31, 1907: On December 31, 1907, the first ball was dropped at Times Square in New York City to celebrate New Year's Eve, beginning a tradition that continues today.
December 31, 1600: On December 31, 1600, the East India Company, formed to exploit trade with East and Southeast Asia and India, was incorporated by English royal charter.
December 31, 1857: On December 31, 1857, Queen Victoria named Ottawa the national capital of Canada.
December 31, 1999: On December 31, 1999, the United States officially handed over control of the Panama Canal to Panama.
December 31, 2004: On December 31, 2004, Taipei 101 opened in Taipei, Taiwan. At 1,667 feet (508 metres), it was then the tallest building in the world.
January 1, 1999: On January 1, 1999, eleven European Union countries adopted the euro as their currency.
January 1, 1804: On January 1, 1804, Haiti declared its independence from France, bringing the Haitian Revolution to an end.
January 1, 1863: On January 1, 1863, US President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation, which freed enslaved people in the Confederacy.
January 1, 1995: On January 1, 1995, the World Trade Organization was formally established.
January 1, 1959: On January 1, 1959, the dictator Fulgencio Batista fled Cuba after his regime was toppled by rebel forces led by Fidel Castro.
